public_rationale: Hallucinations persisted in February 2025: OpenAI's February 27 evaluation reported PersonQA hallucination rates of 0.19 for GPT-4.5, 0.30 for GPT-4o and 0.20 for o1 [e1]. A research paper available May 30, 2024 documents repeated assurances from legal AI providers beginning in 2023 about preventing or mitigating hallucinations [e2]. The evidence also shows qualifications: GPT-4.5 scored better than the comparison models on PersonQA, and its February 27 launch announcement expressed an expectation of fewer hallucinations, without claiming elimination [e1, e3].
limitations: PersonQA is a company-reported, task-specific evaluation; its rates do not establish rates across everyday use.
The documented assurances concern named legal AI providers, not all LLM developers.
The evidence does not measure the frequency implied by 'constant' or establish whether hallucinations can eventually be solved.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Hallucinations have not been solved despite constant assurances that they would be.

statement.excerpt: Hallucinations haven’t solved, despite constant assurances.
statement.document_title: Ezra Klein’s new take on AGI – and why I think it’s probably wrong

our_interpretation: Read the grammatical omission as 'hallucinations have not been solved'.
The ordinary reading is that contemporary LLM systems still generate fabricated or unsupported factual answers in practical use. It does not claim that hallucination rates never improved.
Use February 2025, the latest completed reporting month before the post, for the ongoing model-performance observation.
Read 'constant assurances' as repeated public assurances about preventing or overcoming hallucinations, not a literal uninterrupted stream or a promise by every provider.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary model evaluations document continuing factual hallucinations, while earlier public records establish repeated assurances about preventing or overcoming them.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporary evidence establishes a broadly effective solution to factual hallucinations in the systems under discussion. Improvements or successful narrow safeguards alone do not contradict the claim.
